decisionRationale: The public record verifies that latency, clock mismatch, pose error, calibration error, and independently trained model incompatibility can harm cooperative perception. It does not verify the candidate's residual event: a naturally occurring feature packet from epoch E0 being fused with pose, extrinsic, adapter, or decoder state from epoch E1 during a deployment update.

OpenCOOD and RCP-Bench make related faults injectable, but injectability is not occurrence evidence. RCP-Bench deliberately combines a non-ego camera frame from another timestamp with current metadata; OpenCOOD computes features and transforms in one process and exposes no deployed packet or model-release lineage. Neither asset records a natural cross-epoch tear.

The functional neighborhood is already dense. FreeAlign, CoAlign, Spatial Calibration, SyncNet, LRCP, CoBEVFlow, TraF-Align, CATNet, and STCC address time, pose, or calibration misalignment. HEAL, STAMP, PHCP, PolyInter, GenComm, CodeAlign, and BOLT address heterogeneous or independently trained feature compatibility. RCP-Bench already benchmarks temporal tearing as a synthetic robustness corruption.

ROS 2 atomic parameter services and time synchronizers, DDS coherent sets and XTypes, and ETSI CPM reference-time and sensor metadata provide mature transport, schema, time, and grouping primitives. Without evidence of a cooperative-perception-specific natural failure, the remaining contribution is an epoch/hash manifest plus a reject-or-buffer policy, not a defensible new research object.

The available CPU-only environment cannot execute the required sparse-convolution and CUDA-NMS baselines. A limited GPU can support a narrow synthetic pilot, but the audited releases do not provide a clean two-model rolling-update trace with trustworthy checkpoints and a real transition log. The requested two-week study therefore cannot establish the missing natural significance.
Under the explicit rule that a candidate collapsing to message hashes/epoch fields or lacking natural meaning must be rejected, the decisive outcome is reject rather than revise.

verifiedReferences.title: RCP-Bench: Benchmarking Robustness for Collaborative Perception Under Diverse Corruptions
verifiedReferences.finding: Benchmarks temporal misalignment and diverse corruptions across three datasets and ten models; negative cooperation is an explicit outcome.
verifiedReferences.limitationForCandidate: Its temporal mismatch is a designed corruption, not a recorded rolling-update feature/pose/calibration/model tear.

verifiedReferences.title: TraF-Align: Trajectory-aware Feature Alignment for Asynchronous Multi-agent Perception
verifiedReferences.finding: Treats asynchronous latency as coupled spatial and semantic feature misalignment on V2V4Real and DAIR-V2X-Seq.
verifiedReferences.limitationForCandidate: No discrete model-release or calibration-epoch transition is logged.

verifiedReferences.title: Latency Robust Cooperative Perception Using Asynchronous Feature Fusion
verifiedReferences.finding: Directly fuses asynchronous features and reports robustness at delays up to 500 ms on two datasets.
verifiedReferences.limitationForCandidate: Latency age is studied, but cross-version feature/decoder or calibration tearing is not.

verifiedReferences.title: CATNet: Collaborative Alignment and Transformation Network for Cooperative Perception
verifiedReferences.finding: Jointly compensates temporal latency and multi-source noise, narrowing the candidate's time-plus-pose/calibration space.
verifiedReferences.limitationForCandidate: Does not establish a naturally observed release-epoch tear.

verifiedReferences.title: STCC: Spatiotemporal Co-Sensing Calibration for Robust Cooperative Perception
verifiedReferences.finding: Addresses spatiotemporal calibration under variable delay and prediction.
verifiedReferences.limitationForCandidate: Calibration is numerical and temporal, not a logged software release epoch.

verifiedReferences.title: CoBEVFlow: Flow-based Bird's Eye View Feature Fusion for Asynchronous Collaborative Perception
verifiedReferences.finding: Attributes asynchronous cooperative perception to delay, interruption, and clock mismatch and compensates it with BEV flow.
verifiedReferences.limitationForCandidate: No model or calibration version lineage.

verifiedReferences.title: FreeAlign: Robust Collaborative Perception Without External Localization and Clock Devices
verifiedReferences.finding: Estimates relative pose and time from shared objects without external localization or clocks, using real and simulated data.
verifiedReferences.limitationForCandidate: Shows a route around inaccurate external state, not natural atomicity failure across deployment epochs.

verifiedReferences.title: CoAlign: Robust Collaborative Perception Against Pose Errors
verifiedReferences.finding: Uses pose-graph optimization to correct relative pose errors before feature fusion.
verifiedReferences.limitationForCandidate: Pose errors are continuous numeric errors, not release-state tearing.

verifiedReferences.title: Spatial Calibration for Cooperative Perception

verifiedReferences.limitationForCandidate: No naturally recorded calibration-file update crossing a feature packet.

occupiedSpace: Asynchronous feature compensation and temporal alignment: SyncNet, CoBEVFlow, LRCP, TraF-Align, CATNet, and STCC.
Pose and spatial calibration correction: CoAlign, FreeAlign, Spatial Calibration, CATNet, and STCC.
Heterogeneous model and feature compatibility: HEAL, STAMP, PHCP, PolyInter, GenComm, CodeAlign, and BOLT.
Synthetic robustness benchmarking of temporal mismatch and negative cooperation: RCP-Bench.
Generic atomic grouping, schema evolution, time synchronization, and CPM timing metadata: DDS, DDS-XTypes, ROS 2, and ETSI CPM.
noveltyBoundary.residualClaimTested: A deployment update can naturally produce a received bundle in which feature, pose, extrinsic calibration, adapter, and decoder are individually plausible but belong to different release epochs, causing silent negative cooperation that coherent-stale controls do not explain.
noveltyBoundary.whyResidualIsNotEnough: No reopened primary source records the event, its frequency, or a field consequence. A manifest of capture_time, pose_epoch, extrinsic_hash, encoder_hash, adapter_id, schema_version, bundle_id, and payload_hash is an engineering contract assembled from mature primitives. Without the event, it is not a research contribution.
noveltyBoundary.directPreemptionDetails: RCP-Bench occupies the closest synthetic torn-time benchmark; STAMP/HEAL/BOLT and related works occupy feature compatibility; DDS coherent sets occupy grouped visibility. The candidate's remaining policy is mostly reject, buffer, or select a compatible adapter.

evidence: RCP-Bench fixed code deliberately creates a cross-time camera/metadata inconsistency.
OpenCOOD exposes independent time-delay, spatial-correction, pairwise-transform, encoder, and fusion code paths that can be separated in a custom harness.
Two checkpoints or transform/calibration files can be deliberately crossed and guarded by an epoch/hash manifest.
publicImplementationInjectability.interpretation: These facts prove that a controlled fault can be manufactured. They do not prove that the fault occurs in a deployed cooperative-perception stack.

verifiedAdjacentFacts: V2X-ReaLO measures real online latency and reports degradation associated with asynchronous arrivals, computation, latency, and pose errors.
FreeAlign and Spatial Calibration establish that real or realistic localization and calibration imperfections matter.
BOLT establishes that independently trained feature spaces can make direct fusion worse than ego-only.
missingEvidence: No field incident, release log, ROS bag, packet capture, or dataset contains both producer and consumer model/calibration/pose epoch lineage for a natural transition.
No reopened paper reports feature E0 fused with pose, extrinsic, adapter, or decoder E1 during rolling deployment.
No frequency, duration, or operational pathway for such a transition was established.
naturalOccurrence.effectOnResearchMeaning: The absence is destructive, not a minor gap. Time, pose, calibration, and heterogeneous-model harms are already meaningful research areas; the only allegedly new object is their atomic release pairing. If that pairing is not shown to occur naturally, the candidate becomes a synthetic benchmark plus a message header.

significanceEvidence.decisiveAssessment: Natural relevance for adjacent mismatches survives, but natural relevance for the proposed atomic-bundle event does not. The candidate is therefore rejected rather than reframed around already occupied mismatch problems.

resourceEnvelope.cpuOnly: Available for metadata preparation, manifest/gate unit tests, cached-feature analysis, and jq/report generation. It is not sufficient for decisive OpenCOOD/RCP-Bench inference because the audited stacks require spconv and CUDA NMS.
resourceEnvelope.limitedGpu: A single NVIDIA GPU with 16-24 GB memory could support a narrow inference-only pilot if the legacy CUDA/PyTorch/spconv environment can be built. It does not repair missing natural transition logs or missing trustworthy heterogeneous checkpoints.

strongBaselineSet: CoAlign or FreeAlign numeric pose/calibration correction
SyncNet, LRCP, or TraF-Align temporal compensation
HEAL, STAMP, or BOLT-style compatibility adapter

oracle manifest selecting the correct decoder and calibration state
assetAudit.decisiveFeasibilityFinding: At least two official assets are pinned and injectable, but the available resource envelope supports only a synthetic mechanism pilot. It cannot establish natural occurrence, and the audited compatibility assets do not supply a clean, trustworthy two-model quick baseline.

minimumStudy.purpose: A future re-proposal must isolate a cross-epoch pairing interaction from ordinary stale data. The study does not rescue the rejected candidate without prior natural trace evidence.
minimumStudy.precondition: Obtain a real packet/log corpus containing capture timestamp, arrival timestamp, producer model version, consumer decoder/adapter version, pose source version, extrinsic/calibration version, and deployment transition time. Synthetic execution must not start as a substitute for this precondition.
minimumStudy.pairedUnit: The same scene, same cooperating agent, same source observation, same feature tensor, same feature age, same arrival order, same byte budget, and same ego state, evaluated under counterfactual context assignments.

factorialDesign.componentIsolation: Change exactly one context component per contrast before testing compound tears. Decoder tests keep feature and geometric transforms fixed; pose/calibration tests keep encoder, decoder, and adapter fixed.
factorialDesign.stalenessMatching: Both coherent-stale and torn cells use the identical feature capture time and arrival delay. Temporal compensation is applied identically before the context swap.
factorialDesign.geometryMatching: For pose or extrinsic contrasts, precompute matched perturbation pairs with equal SE(3) error norm relative to the oracle and counterbalanced direction. This prevents a larger numerical perturbation from being mislabeled as atomicity.
factorialDesign.modelMatching: For decoder or adapter contrasts, cache one feature tensor and evaluate it with its declared compatible consumer and the crossed consumer; match parameter count and inference budget where an adapter is used.
factorialDesign.randomization: Randomize cell order within scene and cluster bootstrap by scene, not by agent packet.

datasets: A real online/logged corpus satisfying the precondition; V2X-ReaLO is only usable if release and calibration lineage can be added from original logs.
OPV2V/OpenCOOD or RCP-Bench as a synthetic mechanism replication, never as occurrence evidence.
models: One homogeneous PointPillar/Where2comm-style intermediate-fusion model for geometric tears.
One independently trained or heterogeneous pair with a runnable HEAL/STAMP/BOLT-class compatibility baseline for model tears.
minimumStudy.primaryEstimand: Difference-in-differences interaction: (torn minus its matched coherent state) after subtracting the corresponding current-versus-stale main effect, reported for AP@0.7 and negative-cooperation event rate.
secondaryOutcomes: accepted, buffered, adapted, and rejected packet fractions
minimumStudy.analysisPlan: Report every factorial cell, scene-clustered bootstrap confidence intervals, effect distributions over perturbation magnitude, and the gate's abstention cost. Do not pool stale and torn corruptions.

successCriteria: Before any synthetic result counts, at least one natural deployment transition must contain a verified cross-epoch feature/context pair and a reproducible downstream fusion consequence; a configuration possibility is insufficient.

The preregistered torn-versus-matched-coherent interaction must have a scene-clustered 95% confidence interval entirely on the harmful side and a median AP@0.7 loss of at least 1.0 percentage point for both a geometric tear and a model/decoder tear.
The interaction must replicate in two model families and include at least one real logged dataset; an OPV2V-only or RCP-Bench-only result fails.

A bundle-aware mechanism must reduce accepted harmful torn fusions by at least 80% while retaining at least 80% of valid coherent cooperation and must outperform timestamp-only gating plus the strongest available pose/time/model adapter baseline.

The effect must persist after matching feature age, arrival delay, SE(3) error norm, byte budget, and model inference budget; otherwise it is stale-data or perturbation-magnitude harm, not atomicity harm.
killCriteria: No natural cross-epoch packet is found in a release transition log or field capture. This criterion is already met by the audited public evidence and is the primary reason for rejection.
The only intervention is adding epoch, version, bundle, or hash fields and rejecting mismatches using ordinary DDS/ROS application logic.
Matched coherent-stale and torn cells have no separable interaction after controlling feature age and transform-error norm.
The effect appears only under manually extreme calibration deltas, delays, or incompatible checkpoints outside an observed operational range.
Timestamp synchronization plus CoAlign/FreeAlign or a HEAL/STAMP/BOLT-class adapter closes the apparent gap.
The gate prevents harm only by discarding enough valid messages to lose the benefit of cooperation relative to ego-only or a standard freshness gate.
A second model family or a real logged dataset cannot reproduce the mechanism.
The two-week environment cannot run a trustworthy strong baseline with fixed checkpoints and documented licensing.

controls.definition: Feature, pose, calibration, adapter, and decoder all from E1.
Feature and all matching context from E0, with the same capture age and temporal compensation as the torn cell.
Feature E1 crossed with exactly one E0 context component.
Epoch/hash label is changed while payload, transform, calibration, adapter, and decoder artifacts remain byte-identical; perception output must not change when the gate is disabled.
Change a payload byte outside the consumed tensor and recompute the hash to verify that hash inequality itself is not a perception mechanism.
Coherent and torn geometry conditions receive counterbalanced equal-norm SE(3) errors relative to oracle.
Accept or reject only by capture/arrival age using the same buffering budget.
Use the best runnable HEAL/STAMP/BOLT-class adapter rather than rejecting cross-model features.
No collaborative message is fused; negative cooperation is measured relative to this output.
Select the exactly matching pose, calibration, adapter, and decoder state for each feature packet.

forbiddenClaims: Do not claim that cross-epoch bundle tearing occurs naturally, commonly, or at safety-relevant frequency without a field trace carrying all relevant versions.
Do not infer deployment incidence from OpenCOOD, OPV2V, RCP-Bench, or any manually crossed checkpoint.
Do not call ordinary stale data, timestamp skew, or pose error an atomicity failure unless matched coherent-stale controls isolate a pairing interaction.
Do not claim that ROS 2 or DDS lacks atomic/coherent primitives; the actual gap, if any, is application-level semantic binding and deployment configuration.
Do not claim ETSI CPM noncompliance or insufficiency merely because it lacks neural model hashes; CPM serves a different object-level message contract.
Do not present hashes, epochs, bundle IDs, or schema versions as a novel algorithm or as security guarantees.
Do not claim a reject-only gate improves perception without reporting lost valid cooperation, latency, buffering, and ego-only comparison.
Do not claim CPU-only reproducibility for the audited OpenCOOD/RCP-Bench inference stack.
Do not claim STAMP or HEAL is a ready, trustworthy strong baseline at the audited commits without resolving the documented checkpoint limitations.
Do not extrapolate synthetic detection AP to planning safety, collision reduction, network reliability, or regulatory compliance.
Do not combine model-version mismatch, calibration drift, pose error, and delay into one corruption and attribute the result to atomicity.
Do not use local-corpus records as evidence; they are leads only.
